title: Implementation of MD with Langevin and variable cell shape using Leimkuhler BAOAB integrator
body:
Implementation of Langevin for MD with variable cell shape. Correctly reproduces cell shape fluctuations as confirmed by relation to elastic constants, although test is much too slow to include in CI.

(recreated from original MR using ase repo to take advantage of available runners)

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body:
Thank you for contributing this powerful and useful thermostat!
I took some time last week to look at the papers and get a feel for what is being put together here.

It seems that most of the complexity in the code relates to its ability to work in a number of different regimes:
- nVH
- nVT
- nPH (fixed-shape)
- nPH (variable-shape)
- nPT (fixed-shape)
- nPT (variable-shape)

As well as some handling of default values.

As a general design principle I am wary of parameters that often don't do anything, and of parameters that do special things when given particular floating-point values or ranges.

I think we could remove some nested logic and make things easier to read/maintain by breaking apart into several thermostat classes that have stronger assumptions/requirements about what they are doing. Six is probably too many! Additionally there is the tempting possibility of ABOBA and BAOA variants: 18 classes is definitely too many.

@AndrewRosen @yuzie007 what do you think would fit well with other features? Perhaps three classes: LangevinLeimkuhlerNVT, LangevinLeimkuhlerNPThydrostatic, LangevinLeimkuhlerNPT? With a "structure" parameter switching between "baoab" and "baoa", say. The names do work out a bit verbose :thinking:

We can play around with under-the-hood structure later, but the public API needs to be good the first time.
comments.label_reasoning: General review comment about class design: concerns about parameters that do special things at specific float values and proposal to split into multiple focused classes.

comments.author: noambern
comments.body:
I agree with you about the complexity, and I'd consider refactoring, but I would not split fixed and variable cell - those are distinguished by just a single flag and single simple operation `sigma = np.trace(sigma) / 3 * np.eye()` (in principle - in practice some of the matrix exponential stuff is simplified in the fixed cell shape).

The one down side is that the rest of my workflow is generally more straightforward with being able to use the same constructor and controlling everything with `kwargs`. 

Let me think about it, and follow up here.  I would definitely be interested in hearing other opinions.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Proposes splitting the implementation into multiple thermostat classes with cleaner APIs and a 'structure' parameter.

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body: This parameter doesn't seem to be documented? It's quite unclear why type it should have: `int`, `numpy.random.Generator` or `Callable[int|tuple[int...], np.ndarray]` are all plausible! I think `numpy.random.Generator` is correct? There doesn't seem to be a fallback/default if it is left as `None`; this should call `numpy.random.default_rng()`.
comments.label_reasoning: The `rng` parameter is undocumented in the docstring, its expected type is unclear, and no default is provided.

comments.author: noambern
comments.body: Good point.  Yes, it's used assuming it's a generator. There's no default because I don't believe in doing non-reproducible simulations, so I think it's actively good to _force_ the user to pass something where the seed has been set.  I'd be willing to accept an int, and use it as the seed. I'll clean that up.

comments.author: noambern
comments.body: better in the new version (not yet pushed, should be ready in a few minutes)?

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body: I think the user expectation is that they can run _something_ without worrying about this. I don't mind if the default is deterministic with a fixed seed, though.

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body: As a general rule I'd prefer to let users pass a generator rather than an int, so that things like quasirandom generators to be used instead of the default RNG. (Admittedly QRNG is probably not a brilliant choice for MD. But some people care about using extra-high-quality randomness for Monte Carlo simulations, etc.)

comments.author: noambern
comments.body: It'll now accept a generator or anything that can function as a seed when passed to `np.random.default_rng`, so `int` or one of the other types. But I think a _fixed_ seed is in practice a way more surprising option than allowing for non-deterministic runs (i.e. default seed). Certainly I find `Atoms.rattle`'s behavior https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/blob/master/ase/atoms.py?ref_type=heads#L1490 disastrously surprising. If anything, I'd rather allow non-reproducible runs with defaulting to `np.random.default_rng()`.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Flags missing documentation for a parameter, unclear type, and missing default RNG fallback via `numpy.random.default_rng()`.

comments.author: noambern
comments.body: I'd be willing to do that, grudgingly, but did my claim about non-reproducible simulations convince you?

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body: I do like reproducibility :smile: I think the user-friendly solution is "reproducible by default" rather than "error by default".

comments.author: noambern
comments.body: Except that "reproducible by default" means using the same seed each time, and with Langevin you can lock into identical trajectories by starting with the same seed for the random forces, even if the initial config isn't identical (https://journals.aps.org/pre/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevE.86.026703).

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body: Interesting paper! That does seem a good reason to discourage seed re-use across different runs. (Whereas a default seed would encourage it.)

comments.author: noambern
comments.body: That's my reasoning.  Also, I've already confused myself by not remembering that `Atoms.rattle` uses a fixed seed.

comments.author: noambern
comments.body:
I just pushed an update to all the T/P enabling/disabling stuff.  I think it's now _reasonably_ clean, at least to the extent that's possible without splitting off different classes. I personally like it this way, but I could be convinced to refactor.

Basically, const T and const P (variable cell) are enabled simply by specifying `temperature_K` and  `externalstress`, respectively. All the remaining parameters that control the thermostat and barostat have (hopefully sensible) defaults, and are just ignored if the corresponding functionality isn't enabled.

There's also no longer any overloading of `P_mass == 0` (replaced with `disable_cell_langevin`), and `hydrostatic` defaults to `False`.

The docstring is now more detailed about all of this.

@ajjackson let me know if you think it's an improvement.

comments.author: noambern
comments.body:
I think it's ready, except possibly for the best default behavior when there's no rng passed in. As I said, I'm of the opinion that it's a good idea to force the user to think about it, but if that's not the ASE way, I'll live, but I'm not sure how I feel about the reproducibility - strange behavior tradeoff, so I'm not sure if I'd campaign for fixed seed (reproducible but possible trajectory artifacts) or no seed (not reproducible) passed to default_rng. 

One option that might give the best of both is to use no seed to generate a seed, and then print that seed and use it to initialize the generator.  So the user has, at least in principle, a way of reproducing the run.
